kicker: Two macOS drivers, read from source

scenes.headline: How a computer-use driver spends an agent's time
scenes.sub: Observe, decide, act, and what happens between the beats.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sambar! A new macOS driver says it makes computer-use agents much faster. Where does the time go?

scenes.label: What is new
scenes.text: arc-driver returns the settled next observation inside every action result, so one model turn covers acting and looking.
scenes.say: The idea: every action result carries the settled next view of the window. One model turn covers acting and looking.

scenes.title: The loop every agent runs
scenes.say: Every agent runs the same loop.

items.say: The driver reads the window from the accessibility tree: roles, names, values, actions.
The model decides. That takes seconds.
The driver acts, then waits for the app to finish reacting.

steps.say: The model names a snapshot, an element, and an action. No coordinates.
The driver checks its journal. If a sheet appeared since that snapshot, it refuses and returns a fresh view.
Otherwise it presses the control through accessibility. The pointer never moves.
It counts the app's notifications until they go quiet, then reads the window again.
That fresh snapshot rides back in the same result.

left.title: cua-driver
items: Click polls up to a second for new windows
left.say: cua-driver's click waits up to a second for new windows, so the agent then asks again for the tree and a screenshot.

right.title: arc-driver
right.say: arc-driver settles, refuses stale views, and returns the new snapshot with the action.

scenes.credit: arc-driver's demo video, from the launch post

steps.say: Here it switches System Settings back to Dark.
Dark was already selected, so the app posts nothing, and the driver reports no reaction.

scenes.title: Click to next observation
scenes.note: driver time only, no model in the loop
scenes.say: Driver time alone: about two hundred milliseconds against one and a quarter seconds. Mostly the window poll.

scenes.label: faster on real tasks inside Claude Code, as the author reports
scenes.note: no task list or transcripts published
scenes.say: With a model in the loop, the author reports about one point seven times faster. Fewer model turns is the real win.

scenes.text: Count model calls per action. A driver whose action result is the next observation removes one from every step.
scenes.say: Count model calls per action. A driver whose action result is the next observation removes one per step.

recap: The action result carries the settled view
A refused stale action is safe
Model turns dominate, not the click
scenes.say: To recap: settle and look in one call, refuse stale views, and count model turns.
